title: Signs of a cluttered portfolio, and questions to ask
objectives: Spot five signs of a cluttered portfolio.
body_md:
Signs of a cluttered portfolio: more than 6–8 equity funds for a typical portfolio. Several funds in the same category (for example three large-cap funds). The same 5–10 stocks at the top of most funds. A combined portfolio that looks like an index fund, but with higher costs. Small SIPs of ₹500–₹1,000 spread across many schemes. Questions to ask the client: “Why did you add each fund?”, “Do you hold any shares directly, or through your employer?”, and “Would fewer funds be easier for you to track?”

> **Investor takeaway:** Diversify by what you own, not by how many funds you own.
example: 14 funds with ₹1,000 SIPs each: more paperwork, same top stocks — a cluttered portfolio, not a diversified one.
say: More than 6–8 equity funds for a typical portfolio is a warning sign.
A combined portfolio like an index fund, but costlier, is clutter.
never: Small SIPs across many schemes add diversification.

check.q: Which is a sign of a cluttered portfolio?
o: Three large-cap funds from different AMCs
check.why: Three large-cap funds from different AMCs. Same category, same stocks.
